title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
abstract: arXiv:2610.18651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks. Here, we systematically study the effects of pretraining using a series of such CLMs across 64 molecular property prediction datasets. We find that the downstream gains of pretraining in CLMs do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines. Across the regimes evaluated, only supervised pretraining on traditional physico-chemical descriptors consistently improves downstream performance for the CLMs tested whereas some forms of pretraining result in models worse than a randomly initialized encoder. While models can resolve molecular structure well, they do so no better than a randomly initialized model, suggesting that, at best, CLMs learn descriptor-like properties in addition to low-level token statistics during pretraining, but surprisingly lit

translated_title: 预训练能教会化学语言模型化学吗？
translated_abstract: 化学语言模型（CLM）在大规模分子语料库上进行预训练，旨在学习可迁移到多种下游任务的表示。本研究使用一系列此类化学语言模型，在64个分子性质预测数据集上系统地研究了预训练的效果。我们发现，化学语言模型预训练带来的下游性能提升并不随规模扩大而增长，且性能在低于梯度提升基线的水平上趋于饱和。在所评估的各种预训练模式中，只有在传统理化描述符上进行有监督预训练才能持续提升所测试化学语言模型的下游性能，而某些形式的预训练甚至会导致模型表现不如随机初始化的编码器。尽管模型能够较好地解析分子结构，但其表现并不优于随机初始化的模型，这表明化学语言模型在预训练中充其量只学到了类似描述符的性质和低级token统计信息，而除此之外学到的化学知识出奇地少。
tldr: 化学语言模型的预训练收益无法随规模扩大，性能低于梯度提升基线，仅有基于理化描述符的有监督预训练能持续带来提升，表明预训练几乎未能让模型真正学到化学知识。
en_tdlr: Pretraining gains in chemical language models do not scale and saturate below gradient-boosting baselines, with only supervised pretraining on physico-chemical descriptors consistently improving performance, suggesting CLMs learn surprisingly little chemistry from pretraining.
